chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Ja'far al-Kumaydani narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, linking it through his chain to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).
He said: Four things are done in vain: planting seeds in salty ground, lighting a lamp in the moonlight, eating after satiety, and doing a favor for those who are not worthy of it.
ai.seo_question: What are the four things considered to be done in vain according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq categorizes these four examples of futility to illustrate the principle of *khawab* (vanity), where effort yields no benefit due to mismatched conditions or recipients. This teaching serves as a practical guide for believers to evaluate the wisdom behind their actions, whether in physical endeavors like agriculture or social interactions like charity. It underscores the Shia emphasis on discernment (*tadabbur*) to ensure that one's resources and goodwill are not squandered on the unappreciative or the unsuitable.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-142 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja’far ibn Abi Ja’far al-Kumaydany quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Hikam who linked it up through a chain of narrators to Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB),
“O Ali! Four things are done in vain: eating after (attaining) satiety; lighting a lamp in moonlight; planting seeds in salty ground; and doing a favor for people who are not worthy of it.”
